'''M.G. Finn'''{{r|PolyNetwork}}<!-- his legal first name is "M.G." with NO SPACE see https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182436/https://gtpn.gatech.edu/dr-mg-finn-0 --> (born October 23, 1958) is an American chemist and a Regents' professor at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].

==Early life and education==
Finn was born in [[Atlantic City, New Jersey]], on October 23, 1958.<ref name="thesis-finn-1986" /> He studied chemistry at [[California Institute of Technology]] while receiving a [[Eastman Kodak]] scholarship<ref>{{cite news |title=Scholarships in Chemistry |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=June 15, 1978 |page=SG3 |id={{ProQuest|158574393}}}}</ref> and performing undergraduate research under the direction of [[electrochemist]] Fred C. Anson.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ic50174a064 |title=Electrode reaction pathways for the reduction of chromium(III)-ammine complexes at mercury electrodes |journal=[[Inorganic Chemistry]] |volume=16 |number=8 |pages=2124–2127 |year=1977 |doi=10.1021/ic50174a064 |first1=Fred C. |last1=Anson |first2=M.G. |last2=Finn |first3=Akifumi |last3=Yamada|url-access=subscription }}</ref> After receiving his Bachelor of Science degree in June 1980, Finn spent the summer performing research at [[Eastman Kodak]] in [[Rochester, New York]] before joining the group of future [[Nobel Prize|Nobel prize]] winner, [[Barry Sharpless]], that fall at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he gained his PhD in 1986 with his thesis "On the mechanism of titanium-tartrate catalyzed asymmetric epoxidation".<ref>{{cite web |title=M G Finn |url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=84808 |website=Chemistry Tree |access-date=3 July 2021}}</ref><ref name="thesis-finn-1986">{{cite thesis |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/82731 |title=On the mechanism of titanium-tartrate catalyzed asymmetric epoxidation |date=1986 |institution=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |degree=Ph.D. |last=Finn |first=M.G. |hdl=1721.1/82731 |id={{ProQuest|303453649}} |oclc=14989914}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:2022 Nobel awards ceremony.jpg|thumb|300px|Finn (left) with [[click chemistry]] collaborators [[Barry Sharpless]] (center) and [[Hartmuth C. Kolb]] (right) at the 2022 Nobel awards ceremony]]
After receiving his doctorate, Finn carried out postdoctoral research for two years with [[James P. Collman]] at [[Stanford University]], before joining the faculty of [[University of Virginia]] in 1988. He moved to the [[Scripps Research Institute]] in 1998 (where his former PhD supervisor Barry Sharpless had previously moved to in 1990) and later to [[Georgia Tech]] in 2013,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/science/sdut-scripps-loses-one-worlds-top-ranked-chemists-2012sep18-story.html |title=Scripps loses one of world's top-ranked chemists |first=Gary |last=Robbins |date=September 18, 2012 |newspaper=[[San Diego Union Tribune]]}}</ref> where he currently holds the James A. Carlos Family Chair for Pediatric Technology, and is chief scientific officer of the Children's healthcare of Atlanta Pediatric Technology Center.<ref>{{cite web |title=M.G. Finn Profile |url=https://chemistry.gatech.edu/faculty/finn/ |website=Georgia Tech Chemistry and Biochemistry |access-date=3 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183617/https://chemistry.gatech.edu/faculty/finn/ |archive-date=2021-07-09 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://chemistry.gatech.edu/people/mg-finn |title=M.G. Finn |website=School of Chemistry & Biochemistry |publisher=Georgia Institute of Technology}}</ref><ref name=PolyNetwork>{{cite web |title=M.G. Finn |url=https://gtpn.gatech.edu/dr-mg-finn-0 |website=Georgia Tech Polymer Network |access-date=3 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182436/https://gtpn.gatech.edu/dr-mg-finn-0 |archive-date=2021-07-09 |url-status=live |quote=M.G. (his real first name) obtained his Ph.D. degree in 1986 from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology working with Prof. K.B. Sharpless, followed by an NIH postdoctoral fellowship with Prof. J.P. Collman at Stanford University.}}</ref>

Finn's research concentrates on the development of methods for the synthesis of biologically-important molecules, such as functional virus-like particles. He coined the term [[Click chemistry]] with [[Barry Sharpless]] and [[Hartmuth C. Kolb]]. He also works on the mechanism and optimisation of copper-catalysed azide-alkyl cycloaddition; on targeted synthesis of [[enzyme inhibitors]] and [[antivirals]]; on bio-conjugation and chemical materials science; on the immunology of carbohydrates; and with new methods of enzyme development.

His laboratory works with viruses as building-blocks for targeted development of biologically active molecules.

Finn became the Editor-in-Chief of [[ACS Combinatorial Science]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/pressroom/newsreleases/2010/september/mg-finn-phd-to-head-american-chemical-societys-journal-of-combinatorial-chemistry.html |title=M.G. Finn, Ph.D., to head American Chemical Society's Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry |date=September 1, 2010 |work=[[American Chemical Society]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Editor-in-Chief |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/acsccc/profile.html |journal=[[ACS Combinatorial Science]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521023818/https://pubs.acs.org/page/acsccc/profile.html |archive-date=2016-05-21 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Finn served as chair of the School of Chemistry and Biochemistry from 2013 until 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://chemistry.gatech.edu/news/mgfest-school-celebrates-outgoing-chair-mg-finn |title=At MGFest, School Celebrates Outgoing Chair M.G. Finn |date=October 4, 2024 |work=Georgia Tech School of Chemistry & Biochemistry, College of Sciences}}</ref>

In 2025, Finn was appointed Regents' Professor in the College of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://biosciences.gatech.edu/news/georgia-tech-faculty-and-programs-recognized-2025-regents-awards |title=Georgia Tech Faculty and Programs Recognized With 2025 Regents’ Awards |date=May 22, 2025 |work=
Georgia Tech School of Biological Sciences, College of Sciences}}</ref>

In 2013, [[Thomson Reuters]] suggested that Finn could potentially win a Nobel prize for his ground-breaking work on [[click chemistry]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Robbins |first1=Gary |title=Scripps chemist vies for second Nobel |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/science/sdut-scripps-nobel-sharpless-2013sep24-story.html |newspaper=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |date=September 24, 2013 |access-date=3 July 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Finn's full first name is M.G. He and his wife, Beth, have two children, Allison and Marc.<ref name=PolyNetwork />
